title: Quotients preserve split unipotence over arbitrary fields
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Groups are affine $k$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometrically connected means connected after every field extension. Write $\mathbf G_a(R)=(R,+)$ and $\mathbf G_m(R)=R^\times$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. A represented fppf quotient means a group scheme representing the sheafification of the right-coset functor for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $k$-algebras. A smooth geometrically connected group is split unipotent if it admits a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation with unipotent geometric points and a finite descending series of smooth geometrically connected subgroups, each normal in its predecessor, with represented fppf successive quotients isomorphic to $\mathbf G_a$. Let $U$ be split unipotent, and let $N\subseteq U$ be a smooth geometrically connected normal subgroup. Suppose $Q$ represents the fppf quotient $U/N$, with quotient homomorphism $q:U\to Q$. Then $Q$ is split unipotent over $k$. In particular it has a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation with unipotent geometric points and a finite descending series of smooth geometrically connected subgroups, each normal in its predecessor, whose represented fppf successive quotients are $\mathbf G_a$. There is no perfectness or characteristic restriction on $k$; $N=1$ and $N=U$ are allowed.

source.place: Milne, Algebraic Groups, Section 16g, printed p.343, first paragraph: quotients of split solvable groups are split; Exercise 14-3 gives the additive quotients. Compare Section 14.61--14.62, printed p.299, and Conrad--Lichtenstein, Linear Algebraic Groups I, Example 20.1.6(i), printed pp.52--53. This is a quotient assertion, not the false assertion that all smooth connected subgroups of a split group are split.

proof.text: Choose the given series $U=U_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq U_r=1$. For each $i$, apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] to $U_i\to U\xrightarrow q Q$, obtaining $U_i\xrightarrow{a_i}V_i\hookrightarrow Q$ with $a_i$ faithfully flat, finitely presented, and presenting the fppf quotient by its scheme-theoretic kernel $K_i$. Its hypotheses hold: all schemes are affine of finite type, and hence separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]; $V_i$ is affine because it is closed in $Q$. These are images as sheaves, not just images on $k$-points. Thus $V_{i+1}\subseteq V_i$: locally lift a section of $V_{i+1}$ to $U_{i+1}\subseteq U_i$. Membership in the closed subgroup $V_i$ descends by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], since its inclusion is a monomorphism. As $q$ presents $U/N$, every section of $Q$ lifts fppf locally, so the same argument gives $V_0=Q$. The image of $U_r=1$ is $V_r=1$.

source.place: Section 16g, first paragraph, printed p.343: image of a split series; Theorem 5.39, printed p.108. Separatedness: Stacks Tag 01KN (schemes-lemma-affine-separated); descent: Tag 023Q (descent-lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] to $K_i\triangleleft U_i$. By Step 1, $V_i$ represents precisely $U_i/K_i$, so the lemma implies that $V_i$ is smooth. For every field extension $L/k$, quotient formation commutes with extension and the connected scheme $(U_i)_L$ surjects onto $(V_i)_L$; the connected-quotient clause over $L$ gives connectedness of $(V_i)_L$. Thus every $V_i$ is connected after every field extension of $k$. No $K_i=U_i\cap N$ has been assumed smooth or connected.

source.place: Section 16g, printed p.343; Definition 14.61 and paragraph 14.62, printed p.299; quotient smoothness and connectedness in Proposition 1.62 and Proposition 5.59.

proof.text: For $v\in V_i(A)$ and $w\in V_{i+1}(A)$, take a common fppf refinement on which $v=a_i(u)$ and $w=a_{i+1}(h)$ for $u\in U_i$ and $h\in U_{i+1}$. Normality of $U_{i+1}$ in $U_i$ gives $uhu^{-1}\in U_{i+1}$, so $vwv^{-1}$ lies locally in $V_{i+1}$. Descent of this membership, again [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], gives $V_{i+1}\triangleleft V_i$ over every algebra. The local lifts are supplied by [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization]. Now [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] supplies the affine finite-type represented quotient $R_i=V_i/V_{i+1}$, with quotient map $b_i$ and scheme-theoretic kernel $V_{i+1}$.

source.place: Section 16g, printed p.343, taking images of the subnormal series; Theorem 5.39 and Theorem 5.55, printed pp.108,113; descent is Stacks Tag 023Q (descent-lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms).

proof.text: The composite $b_i a_i:U_i\to R_i$ kills $U_{i+1}$. It is therefore constant on its right cosets and factors through the given quotient $U_i/U_{i+1}\simeq\mathbf G_a$, giving $c_i:\mathbf G_a\to R_i$. This uses exactly the universal property of sheafification in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; representable targets are sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. The group identities descend along the locally surjective quotient map. Every section of $R_i$ locally lifts first to $V_i$ and then to $U_i$, by [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] and Step 1, hence locally belongs to the image of $c_i$. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] to $c_i$. Its closed image is all $R_i$, since every section locally belongs to that image and membership descends. Consequently $c_i$ presents $R_i$ as the fppf quotient $\mathbf G_a/H_i$ for the closed subgroup scheme $H_i=\ker(c_i)$.

source.place: Section 16g, printed p.343, successive quotients are quotients of the original factors; Proposition 5.21, printed p.104, and Theorem 5.39, printed p.108. Sheafification: Stacks Tag 00WH (sites-proposition-sheafification-adjoint).

proof.text: If $H_i=\mathbf G_a$, its coset sheaf is the one-element sheaf, so $R_i=1$. Otherwise [lem-sfb-additive-subgroup-polynomial-quotient] gives $\mathbf G_a/H_i\simeq\mathbf G_a$ over $k$, hence $R_i\simeq\mathbf G_a$. The lemma allows arbitrary proper subgroup schemes, including nonreduced or disconnected ones. When $R_i=1$, its kernel description in Step 3 gives $V_i=V_{i+1}$. Delete just these repetitions from the finite chain. Each remaining inclusion is one of the previous normal inclusions, with quotient $\mathbf G_a$; all terms remain smooth and geometrically connected by Step 2. If all terms coincide, the chain is $Q=1$ with length zero.

source.place: Section 16g, printed p.343, and Exercise 14-3(a), printed p.301, with Definition 14.61, printed p.299.

proof.text: It remains to verify the matrix clause without assuming a quotient representation of $U$ remains faithful. The trivial group embeds in $\mathcal U_{1,k}$; $\mathbf G_a$ embeds in $\mathcal U_{2,k}$ by $x\mapsto\begin{pmatrix}1&x\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$. This map is closed since the induced coordinate map is onto [def-sc-gm-ga, def-sc-general-linear-group, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Induct upwards along the chain of Step 5: the base is its last, trivial term; at each preceding term the kernel is the already treated successor and the quotient is $\mathbf G_a$. All groups are affine of finite type, the successor is closed normal, and the quotient is the represented fppf quotient with that kernel. Thus [lem-sfb-unipotent-extension-arbitrary] gives a closed embedding of this term into some $\mathcal U_{n,k}$. At the first term this embeds $Q$ faithfully into $\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$. For an upper unitriangular matrix, any nonzero summand in an entry of $(g-I)^n$ would require $n+1$ strictly increasing indices in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$; there are none. Thus every geometric point is unipotent. This representation, Step 2, and Step 5 give precisely split unipotence as stated, including $N=1$ and $N=U$.

source.place: Definition 14.61 and paragraph 14.62, printed p.299; Theorem 14.5(b) and Corollary 14.7 (extensions), printed pp.281--282; Section 16g, printed p.343.

proof_origin.place: Section 16g, first paragraph, printed p.343: take images of a split series, use Exercise 14-3(a), printed p.301, and remove trivial factors. The representation clause is assembled using Corollary 14.7 (extensions), printed p.282.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q90-87c891436 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: First split of a proofless item (not a 2026-10-21 re-split). The statement is unchanged and there are no new nodes. The proof follows Milne iAG2017 §16g p.343 (quotients of split groups are split, via Exercise 14-3(a) p.301; Def 14.61/14.62 p.299), which I read in the local PDF. Steps: (1) the images V_i of U_i in Q come from the homomorphism-factorization node, with separatedness from affine-source-separated and membership descending by fpqc representable descent; V_0=Q because q is the fppf quotient. (2) V_i=U_i/K_i is smooth and connected after every field extension, by the affine-normal-quotient node. Its geometric connectedness is defined through k-bar, but the gap is bridged by base change to each L. K_i is not assumed smooth. (3) Normality is proved by local lifts and descent, and gives R_i=V_i/V_{i+1} with kernel V_{i+1}. (4) b_i a_i factors through U_i/U_{i+1}≅Ga by the universal property of sheafification, and is locally surjective, so the factorization node gives R_i≅Ga/H_i. (5) The additive-polynomial node handles any proper H_i, including nonreduced or étale ones; repeated terms are deleted correctly. (6) Unipotent-extension permanence, by upward induction from 1 and Ga⊂U_2, gives a closed embedding into U_n; the nilpotence count is elementary. Small cases checked: N=1, N=U, U=Ga, and alpha_p or Artin-Schreier kernels. Duplicate search (rg -L for split unipotent or solvable) found only the definition, the Rosenlicht criterion, the perfect-field series, permanence, and the consumer, so no duplicates; there is no cycle. Batch-5: the four new citations reach sec-trace-formula only through fppf base change, fppf-is-fpqc (Mathlib leaves) and the scheme descent-datum definition. These are general site infrastructure, not the trace formula or Poincaré duality or a step of their proofs, so they are accepted. No fixes, no tool_uses.
